title: USDS converts to USDC only by routing through DAI and the legacy PSM
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.4.1 walks through `swapUSDSToUSDC` and it is a two-hop path. First, "USDS is swapped to DAI in a 1:1 ratio through the `daiUsds` contract." Then "DAI is swapped to USDC in the PSM at a 1:1 ratio with no fee, using the `buyGemNoFee` function." `swapUSDCToUSDS` runs the same route in reverse, and the amounts are converted between 18 and 6 decimals via `psmTo18ConversionFactor`.

USDS has no direct USDC facility of its own. Its dollar convertibility is inherited from DAI's Peg Stability Module, with the `daiUsds` contract acting as a 1:1 bridge between the new unit and the old one. Even the revert string is legacy: `DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill`.

The upside is that this reuses the most battle-tested piece of the ecosystem's peg machinery, at zero fee, rather than building a new one. USDS gets DAI's stability guarantees on day one.

The cost is a dependency chain on the critical path. Every USDS↔USDC conversion passes through two additional contracts, and both the 1:1 swap and the PSM's no-fee redemption must hold for the route to work as documented. Anything that impairs DAI's PSM — depletion, deprecation, a parameter change introducing a fee — propagates directly into Spark's ability to source USDC, which is the asset most of its external venues actually need.
description: swapUSDSToUSDC swaps USDS to DAI 1:1 via the daiUsds contract, then DAI to USDC through the PSM's buyGemNoFee at 1:1 with no fee — inherited Maker plumbing on the critical path.
